categories.statement_repair: The pinned/rendered FORMAL STATEMENT of a fact or claim was itself wrong, drifted, or internally inconsistent, and the work was to correct the statement's identity/text rather than to prove or disprove it. Distinguishes 'we proved (or graded) the wrong sentence' from proof difficulty.
categories.missing_definitions: A target could not even be stated or attempted until a new constructive definition, datatype, or fundamental operation existed in the kernel prelude. Includes the mandatory evaluation test, since the kernel's type-check cannot certify a Definition's meaning, only its type.
categories.retrieval: Effort spent determining whether needed infrastructure (a lemma, a helper, an entire theorem, a producer) already exists in the tree before writing anything new, including verifying or refuting a prior lane's 'blocked on X' handoff claim. Success here looks like doing LESS work, not more.
categories.proof_assembly: Constructing the actual kernel proof term for a statement already known to be true and stateable: chaining lemmas, inductions, case splits, congruence obligations. The mathematical core the D1-D4 roadmap is aimed at accelerating.
categories.kernel_debugging: Diagnosing a kernel-term-level failure (TypeMismatch, UnboundFVar, non-reduction, stack overflow) or exercising the kernel's own soundness via differential/mutation testing against an independent reference (pinned Lean). About the mechanics of what the kernel accepts or rejects, not about mathematical truth.
categories.semantic_falsification: Checking whether a proposed statement is actually TRUE, independent of the kernel: numeric counterexamples, vacuous-control detection, false/valid/vacuous fixture classification. Runs before proof effort is spent, or accounts for effort already wasted on a false target.
categories.safety_evidence: Building, auditing, or repairing the machinery that measures and credits TRUST itself: safety-matrix columns, statement-identity pins, duplicate-proposition audits, held-out isolation, mutation kill tables for ledger-level guards, external attestation, and adversarial audits of the project's own claims.
categories.integration: Wiring newly-finished work into the shared surface for the FIRST time: registering a gate in justfile/check.sh, merging a sibling lane's branch, joining one lane's artifact to another's so downstream consumers can use it.
categories.infrastructure_maintenance: Repairing EXISTING shared infrastructure that had gone stale, wrong, or broken since it was first built: a CI gate red from a merge nobody re-ran, a script archived out from under its own citations, a stale pinned count, a guard whose premise was simply false. Reactive repair of decay, distinct from integration (first-time wiring of new work) and from safety_evidence (building new trust measurement).

category_additions.infrastructure_maintenance: Not one of the D0 spec's eight named categories. Added because a large, mechanically recurring share of the sampled episodes (gate-rot reproductions, archived-script provenance breaks, a false premise about Python import mechanics) is neither a first-time integration nor a new safety measurement -- it is repair of decay in infrastructure that already existed and had already been trusted. Stretching 'integration' or 'safety_evidence' to cover it would blur exactly the distinction this taxonomy exists to keep sharp; see the D0 report for the measured share this category carries.
